name: PA1010D Mini GPS module
description: CDtop PA1010D GNSS receiver (MediaTek MT3333, GPS + GLONASS, built-in 10 mm ceramic patch antenna) that streams NMEA 0183 sentences (position, altitude, speed, UTC time) over a UART at 9600 baud 8N1, once per second by default; with GPS+GLONASS the talker is GN ($GNGGA, $GNRMC). The module itself runs on 3.0-4.3 V; the breakout's AP2112K regulator lets it run from 3.3-5 V, RXI and I2C are level shifted, TXO is 3.3 V logic. It also has an I2C interface (address 0x10) that this part does not use. Sold as: Adafruit Mini GPS PA1010D - UART and I2C - STEMMA QT (product 4415), two 6-pin headers (VIN, 3Vo, GND, SCL, SDA, Rst / GND, PPS, VIN, RXI, TXO, WAKE) plus two STEMMA QT sockets and a CR1220 holder footprint.
eli5: A tiny GPS with its antenna on top: it listens to satellites and tells your board where on Earth it is, once a second.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply, 3.3-5 V into the on-board AP2112K 3.3 V regulator (first header, pin 1). Use a quiet supply: the GPS needs under 50 mVpp ripple

pins.name: 3Vo
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (about 100 mA spare); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (module answers at 0x10); 10 kOhm pull-up and level shifter on the board. Not used in UART mode, leave unconnected

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (module answers at 0x10); 10 kOhm pull-up and level shifter on the board. Not used in UART mode, leave unconnected

pins.name: RST
pins.description: Reset, active low (printed Rst); pulled up on the board. Leave unconnected for normal use

pins.name: GND2
pins.description: Second ground pin, first pin of the other header (printed GND)

pins.name: PPS
pins.description: One pulse per second output (2.8 V CMOS), synchronised to GPS time; also drives the red PPS LED. Optional

pins.name: VIN2
pins.description: Second VIN pin on the other header (printed VIN), same net as VIN; one supply connection is enough

pins.name: RXI
pins.description: Module serial input, level shifted (3-5 V logic): connect to the board's UART TX. Only needed to send PMTK commands

pins.name: TXO
pins.description: Module serial output, NMEA at 9600 baud 8N1, 3.3 V logic (2.4-2.8 V high): connect to the board's UART RX

pins.name: WAKE
pins.description: WAKE-UP input, active high: wakes the module from backup mode. Leave unconnected for normal use

buildNotes: The board has two 6-pin headers on opposite edges; wire it with jumper leads. You only need VIN, GND and TXO (plus RXI to send commands).
Cross the serial lines: TXO goes to the board's UART RX pin; RXI (optional) to the board's UART TX pin.
Default is 9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit; open the UART at 9600 or the sentences come out as garbage.
TXO is 3.3 V logic (2.4-2.8 V high), fine for ESP32 and Pico; RXI and SDA/SCL are level shifted so 5 V boards can drive them.

The antenna is the square ceramic block on top: keep it facing the open sky. A cold start takes about 35 s outdoors (60 s max); indoors it may never get a fix. The red PPS LED blinks once a second when there is a fix.
Default sentences start $GNGGA / $GNRMC (GPS+GLONASS), not $GPGGA, so match the sentence type after the 2-letter talker.
Power it from a quiet 3.3 V or 5 V pin (ripple under 50 mVpp); it draws about 36 mA while acquiring, 28 mA tracking.
Fit a CR1220 cell in the holder on the back to keep satellite data between power-ups for 1 s hot starts.

test.title: Reports the position and altitude set on the sliders

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (6 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
